bib.title: What does BERT look at? An Analysis of BERT's Attention
bib.venue: Proceedings of the Second BlackboxNLP Workshop on Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP, pages 276-286

question: What do the attention heads of a pre-trained BERT model attend to, and do they correspond to linguistic notions of syntax and coreference?
hypothesis: Attention heads learned by self-supervised pre-training encode some syntactic and coreference structure without explicit supervision.
contributions: Analysis methods for attention maps of pre-trained models, applied to BERT
Surface-level patterns: delimiter tokens, positional offsets, broad attention; heads in a layer behave similarly
Individual heads that match specific dependency relations and coreference
An attention-based probing classifier that reaches 77 UAS on dependency parsing

method.summary: Attention maps are extracted from frozen BERT-base and analysed three ways: surface statistics (attention to special tokens, offsets, entropy, gradients), each head treated as a no-training classifier that predicts the most-attended word for syntactic relations and coreference, and small trained probes over all heads' attention for dependency parsing. A final section clusters heads by Jensen-Shannon distance.
method.task: analysis of attention in pre-trained BERT-base (dependency parsing, coreference probes)

datasets.name: Wikipedia segments
datasets.preprocessing: each segment at most 128 tokens, two consecutive paragraphs, input [CLS]<paragraph-1>[SEP]<paragraph-2>[SEP]

datasets.name: Penn Treebank WSJ with Stanford Dependencies
datasets.split: head analysis (Table 1): not stated; probe results on the dev set; probe trained on train set
datasets.preprocessing: token-to-word attention: sum over tokens of a split-up target word, mean over tokens of a split-up source word; about 8% of words are split; [SEP] and [CLS] ignored

other.pretraining: 3.3 billion tokens of unlabeled text, masked LM and next sentence prediction
other.uncased: a similar [SEP] pattern appears in the uncased model (not shown)

models.name: Attention-only probe
models.params: weight vectors w and u, one entry per head per direction (2 x 144)
models.architecture: p(i|j) proportional to exp(sum_k w_k a_ij^k + u_k a_ji^k)

other.bert_frozen: BERT attention outputs fixed, no backprop into BERT

models.name: Attention-and-words probe
models.architecture: p(i|j) proportional to exp(sum_k W_k,:(v_i concat v_j) a_ij^k + U_k,:(v_i concat v_j) a_ji^k), v = fixed GloVe

training.objective: supervised head prediction: probability distribution over candidate head words for each word (graph-based dependency parser)

other.note: only the probe parameters are trained; the paper gives no training hyperparameters

inference.decoding: per word, the other word receiving the most attention weight is the prediction
inference.samples: single pass over the data, no seeds stated

parameters.fixed_offset_baseline: predicts the head at a fixed offset, best offset per relation shown in parentheses
parameters.head_distance: sum over tokens in data of Jensen-Shannon divergence between two heads' attention distributions, embedded by multidimensional scaling (Kruskal, 1964)
parameters.gradient_importance: magnitude of gradient of BERT masked-LM loss w.r.t. each attention weight (Sundararajan et al., 2017)

metrics.name: Accuracy per dependency relation
metrics.definition: share of words of that relation for which the most-attended word is the gold head/dependent (best direction)

metrics.name: UAS
metrics.definition: unlabeled attachment score of head prediction on WSJ

metrics.name: Antecedent selection accuracy
metrics.definition: percent of time the head word of a coreferent mention most attends to the head of one of that mention's antecedents

metrics.name: Attention entropy
metrics.definition: average entropy of a head's attention distribution

baselines: nearest mention with same head word
rule-based multi-pass sieve system (Lee et al., 2011)
probe on randomly initialized BERT with pretrained word/positional embeddings
eval.protocol: no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests reported; best head chosen on the same data it is scored on

limits: Only BERT-base analysed; one run, no seeds or significance tests reported.
The authors say they would not claim individual heads capture dependency structure as a whole; many relations only slightly beat the fixed-offset baseline.
Best head per relation is picked on the same data it is scored on.
The no-op account of [SEP] attention is speculation supported by small gradients, not an intervention.
The structural probe comparison is not like for like.
The authors cite Jain and Wallace (2019) on attention not being explanation and Michel et al. (2019) on prunable heads; they study what attention holds, not what drives predictions.
Probe training hyperparameters are not given.
